A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same latent-thought pretraining work, renamed PonderLM-2 in v3. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original pretraining, downstream evaluation, continual-pretraining and ablation results, including additional architecture-scaling experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds test-time scaling evaluations, convergence diagnostics, component ablations and latent-thought decoding analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed hidden-state feedback, token-thought interleaving, Jacobi updates, next-token loss and reused positional IDs remain unchanged. PonderLM-2 is a rename. The changed iteration-count range is a training-setting revision; the newly tested component variants are ablations.

E1.justification: V3 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning and TruthfulQA generative question answering, evaluated with test-time scaling strategies (Section 4.5 and Appendix C). These materially extend the original language-modeling, general downstream and instruction-following coverage. The larger-model ablations otherwise reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds TinyLLaMA to the training-compute scaling comparison; v1's scaling panels compare against Pythia. Existing baseline families in the downstream and controlled LLaMA comparisons remain. The additional seven-step PonderLM condition changes its computational setting rather than introducing a new method family.

E3.justification: The reported Jacobi sampling range changes from {2, 3, 4} to {2, 3}, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New protocols include voting and Best-of-N with 1–10 samples, CoT comparisons, EM/ROUGE-L evaluation, LLaMA-410M ablations trained on 6B tokens, and a seven-step PonderLM condition with 8× inference FLOPs.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands convergence diagnostics beyond v1's vanilla-model MSE curve, including agreement with sequential inference and fixed-versus-randomized iteration counts. Appendices G–J add larger-model thought-chain scaling, isolated representation/Jacobi/interleaving ablations, memory trade-offs and qualitative plus quantitative latent-decoding probes.

E5.justification: Figure 9 and Appendix D.2 add explicit log-linear estimation of convergence decay rates and corresponding R-squared statistics; v1's convergence analysis only plots MSE. Neither version reports repeated-training seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Test-time sample counts are inference budgets, not repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 4 and the relocated detailed downstream table retain their numerical results. Substantial new results include GSM8K CoT EM of 32.90% versus 24.26% for Standard CPT, and LLaMA-410M average accuracy increasing from 39.7% to 44.9% across zero to five latent thoughts. Additional comparator, convergence, ablation and decoding results extend the evidence rather than demonstrate same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix D introduce a causal finite-step convergence argument, stabilization within at most T iterations, contraction-based geometric and posterior error bounds, and an argument for equivalence with sequential inference. V1 specifies the iteration but provides no corresponding theoretical development. The fast-rate bounds depend on a contraction assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: general-corpus pretraining with per-token latent thoughts, superiority to doubled-parameter models at matched inference cost, and benefits from longer latent-thought chains. Renaming and additional supporting studies do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of latent thoughts as preliminary hypotheses followed by verification, test-time sampling as evidence of candidate diversity, and fixed-depth training as causing depth overfitting. It also explicitly discusses approximately 8× training FLOPs, doubled KV-cache storage and preservation of positional context capacity, materially expanding the account of mechanisms and trade-offs.

D1.justification: V3 supplies explicit code and model-checkpoint links, replacing v1's supplementary-code statement and promise of a future public repository. It additionally documents 73,047 GPU-hours on 64GB GPUs, training-FLOPs accounting, BFloat16 precision and the doubled-depth construction of the 2.8B comparator. External resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: Narayanan et al. (2021) is removed from the introduction and bibliography. The substantive positioning against Coconut, PonderLM, depth-sharing approaches and discrete thinking-token methods, including the taxonomy, remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites method and evaluation explanations, converts baseline lists into consolidated prose, and reorganizes the efficiency discussion around training and inference costs. It standardizes PonderLM-2 terminology and restructures the appendices: v1's substantive Appendices D–E become A–B, while its declaration sections disappear. These changes extend beyond adding scientific results.

P2.justification: The document adopts a new visual template with colored headings, a shaded abstract and revised running headers. Figure 1 gains a training-FLOPs panel, Figure 2 gains a causal-dependency diagram, and the convergence display becomes a two-panel logarithmic analysis. Several new plots and tables accompany the added studies; retained displays are also relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important gaps in v1 through component-isolating ablations, stronger training-compute comparisons and diagnostics connecting parallel training to sequential inference. These additions substantially strengthen the evidence and cost transparency, while resource links improve reproducibility information. The fast-convergence argument remains conditional on contraction, which empirical fits alone do not establish, and repeated-run uncertainty remains absent. These limitations temper but do not outweigh the gains.
